text: The language, customs, and beliefs that a group of people share are part of its: A) economy B) environment C) culture D) government
For thousands of years, people have passed on their values, ideas, and traditions mainly through: A) radio and television B) newspapers and magazines C) books and movies D) legends and folktales
Both the United States and Mexico are located on the continent of: A) North America B) South America C) Africa D) Europe
What is the name given to the study of climate, landforms, bodies of water, and natural resources of a specific place? A) civics B) geography C) economics D) history

Earth's surface is divided into climate zones: high latitudes (near the poles, between the Arctic/Antarctic Circle and the pole), middle latitudes, and low latitudes (near the equator, between the tropics). In which part of the world will you find the coldest weather? A) between the tropic of Cancer and the equator B) between the Antarctic Circle and the South Pole C) between the Arctic Circle and the tropic of Cancer D) between the equator and the tropic of Capricorn

Using the same climate zone system (high latitudes near poles, middle latitudes, low latitudes near equator, each split into northern and southern halves by the equator), in which climate zone is the continental United States located? A) northern middle latitudes B) northern low latitudes C) southern high latitudes D) southern middle latitudes

A child's breakfast includes: cantaloupe from Guatemala, corn flakes and milk from the United States, cocoa from Ghana, and a banana from Ecuador. What does this show about the people in her community? A) they depend on other world communities to meet their needs and wants B) they often live with people from other cultural groups C) they rely on local products D) they have many different customs and traditions
The money a worker is paid is called a: A) tax B) wage C) price D) barter
The elected official in charge of running a city is called a: A) duchess B) governor C) mayor D) prime minister
Local governments are important because they make decisions for the: A) community B) state C) nation D) world

In an Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) village council: Council Leaders make plans and decisions; Clan Mothers appoint council leaders; Respected Older People give advice; Village Members attend councils and have the right to speak. As part of the council, village members have the right to: A) appoint council leaders B) make decisions C) make council plans D) speak at council meetings

European explorers, including Verrazano and Cartier, explored North America because they were trying to: A) claim land for England B) find out who lived there C) find a shorter trade route to Asia D) trade with Native American Indians
Early Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) villages were usually located near: A) streams B) deserts C) mountains D) oceans
In which type of home did the early Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) most often live? A) igloo B) teepee C) cabin D) longhouse
Which term is defined as a settlement ruled by another country? A) state B) village C) region D) colony

Which person wrote much of the Declaration of Independence, was a political leader during the Revolution, and later became president of the United States? A) Benjamin Franklin B) Thomas Jefferson C) Patrick Henry D) Abraham Lincoln

What was the main reason there were many Africans in the early American colonies? A) they were forced to come to America as slaves B) they wanted farmland not available in Africa C) they were searching for religious freedom D) they wanted to live in a place with democracy
skill: history - the transatlantic slave trade and colonial America

text: In the 1660s, most people living in the Dutch colonial settlement of New Amsterdam came from: A) Africa B) The Netherlands C) Great Britain D) France
skill: history - Dutch colonization of New Amsterdam (now New York)

text: A timeline shows: 1775 Revolutionary War begins; 1776 Declaration of Independence signed; 1777 New York State adopts its constitution AND the Articles of Confederation are written and sent to the states; 1781 Articles of Confederation approved by all 13 states, British surrender; 1783 peace treaty signed; 1787 US Constitution written; 1788 US Constitution approved; 1789 new government begins; 1791 Bill of Rights becomes part of the Constitution. In which year did New York State adopt its constitution? A) 1777 B) 1787 C) 1789 D) 1791
skill: history - reading a timeline of Revolutionary-era events

text: Using the same timeline as the previous question (1775 war begins; 1776 Declaration signed; 1777 NY constitution and Articles of Confederation written; 1781 Articles approved, British surrender; 1783 peace treaty signed; 1787 Constitution written; 1788 Constitution approved; 1789 new government begins; 1791 Bill of Rights added), which statement is true? A) The Declaration of Independence was signed before the Revolutionary War began B) The Bill of Rights was included in the original United States Constitution C) The Americans and British signed the peace treaty to end the Revolutionary War before the Constitution was written D) The Articles of Confederation and the Constitution were approved the same year
skill: history - interpreting chronological relationships on a timeline

text: What is one way to help conserve New York's resources? A) driving a car instead of walking B) washing a car every day C) shutting the light off when leaving a room D) using air conditioners on hot days

Why was the Erie Canal important to the United States? A) it connected the Great Lakes to the St. Lawrence River B) it gave immigrants an easier route to New York City C) it was supported by Governor De Witt Clinton D) it provided an easier, faster, and more direct way to ship goods
skill: NY state history - the Erie Canal's economic significance

text: In which order, from earliest to latest, did major forms of transportation in New York State develop? A) steamboat, automobile, train, plane B) steamboat, train, automobile, plane C) train, steamboat, plane, automobile D) automobile, steamboat, plane, train
What do the stripes on the United States flag symbolize? A) strength and character B) honesty and commitment C) the original thirteen colonies D) the months of the year
skill: civics - symbolism of the US flag

text: On which day does the United States especially honor soldiers who died for their country in wartime? A) Memorial Day B) Independence Day C) Labor Day D) Martin Luther King Jr. Day
skill: civics - national holidays and their meaning

text: A census is taken every ten years in the United States to determine a state's: A) location B) customs C) traditions D) population

The highest and most important court in the United States is called the: A) District Court of Northern New York B) United States Court of Appeals C) United States Supreme Court D) New York State Court of Appeals
Saying the Pledge of Allegiance, respecting the American flag, and celebrating on the Fourth of July are all examples of: A) disloyalty B) sectionalism C) patriotism D) poor citizenship

National, state, and local governments in the US are called representative governments. What is the role of citizens in a representative government? A) they participate directly in all government decisions B) they have no say in government decisions C) they elect federal judges who then appoint government leaders D) they elect government officials who make decisions for them
On a world map, which two continents are located entirely south of the equator? A) Europe and Africa B) Africa and Australia C) Australia and Antarctica D) Asia and South America

A passage reads: '...The United States Constitution can be changed by adding new laws called amendments. Three-fourths of the states must ratify [approve] an amendment for it to be added to the Constitution. The first ten amendments are called the Bill of Rights. People should know what each amendment means. I believe the Bill of Rights contains the most important amendments to the Constitution...' Which one of these sentences from the passage is an opinion? A) The United States Constitution can be changed by adding new laws called amendments B) Three-fourths of the states must ratify an amendment for it to be added to the Constitution C) The first ten amendments are called the Bill of Rights D) I believe the Bill of Rights contains the most important amendments to the Constitution
skill: critical reading - distinguishing fact from opinion
